probe: m7-probe5: how the profiler may derive a pass descriptor that carries timestampWrites (finding C8 of the adversarial review wf_c06a8209-415)
machine: Apple M2 Pro (16-core GPU) / Metal, Chrome 154.0.8037.58, chrome-devtools-gpu server (--enable-webgpu-developer-features), page http://localhost:5173/?mode=B&bench
method: One device with timestamp-query, one query set, one command encoder. Each case opens a pass through a derived descriptor, draws a full-screen triangle (render) or dispatches 64 workgroups (compute), then the set is resolved and read back. A validation error scope wraps the encoding and the submit.

derivations.viaCreate: Object.create(desc ?? {}, { timestampWrites: { value: tw, enumerable: true } })
derivations.viaProxyOnDesc: new Proxy(desc ?? {}, { get(target, key) { return key === 'timestampWrites' ? tw : Reflect.get(target, key, target); } })

results.0 render class via Object.create: THROWS TypeError: Cannot read private member #view from an object whose class did not declare it
results.5 frozen literal with explicit undefined: THROWS TypeError: Failed to execute 'beginRenderPass' on 'GPUCommandEncoder': Failed to read the 'timestampWrites' property from 'GPURenderPassDescriptor': 'get' on proxy: property 'timestampWrites' is a read-only and non-configurable data property on the proxy target but the proxy did not return its actual value (expected 'undefined' but got '#<Object>')

run2.derivation: const source = desc ?? {}; new Proxy({}, { get: (_target, key) => (key === 'timestampWrites' ? tw : Reflect.get(source, key, source)) }) — a FRESH empty target, so no Proxy invariant can bind

conclusions: Object.create makes the caller's descriptor the PROTOTYPE of the one the browser reads, so an inherited accessor runs with the derived object as `this`: a class descriptor whose getter reads a #private field throws, inside beginRenderPass, only while profiling (C8).
A Proxy whose target is the caller's descriptor keeps the receiver, but a frozen descriptor with an own `timestampWrites: undefined` violates the Proxy get invariant and throws.

A Proxy over a fresh empty object that reads every member from the caller with the caller as receiver works in every case: WebIDL dictionary conversion reads members with [[Get]] only, and Chrome accepts a Proxy there. The caller's descriptor is never written.
